study type: Retrospective cohort study using population-based registry data
cohort: The study analyzed 22,744 patients diagnosed with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) in the United States, identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) registry between 1975 and 2012.
finding: The incidence of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) continues to increase, particularly in older adults, with more recent generations showing higher incidence rates than older generations.
